spark.scene: True-color satellite view of the Hawaiian Islands chain from the northwest islands to the large island in the southeast, with scattered bright white cumulus and cirrus clouds over ocean and islands and dark open ocean between.

plumes.label: thin pale blue-gray streak south of the large island
plumes.visual_description: diffuse pale blue-gray translucent veil extending southward from the southern tip of the large island over dark ocean, distinct in color and texture from surrounding bright white clouds

evidence: USGS HVO at image time: Kilauea ADVISORY/YELLOW in episodic_pause with Episode 55 ending 9:03 a.m. HST Oct 17, while Mauna Loa NORMAL/GREEN not erupting, favoring Kilauea as vog source. [E1]

Summit wind from NNE (30 deg at 16.7 km/h) blows toward SSW, consistent with pale veil extending southward from southern tip; downstream plume wind from ENE (71 deg at 37.8 km/h) continues southwestward transport. [E7, E2]
Wind-aligned plume geometry: upwind end 50.3 km from Kilauea summit vs 69.0 km from Mauna Loa summit, centroid ~100 km south, 142-km veil, closer to and downwind of Kilauea. [E6, E3]

Mask is 96.6% ocean (land_frac 0.034, minimal Hawaii overlap, no island swallowed), supporting over-water haze; visual pale blue-gray translucent veil distinct from surrounding bright white cumulus/cirrus. [E4]
No FIRMS fire clusters in plume bbox, excluding local wildfire smoke; strong Kilauea-summit volcanic thermal (316 marker pixels) confirms hot source persisting through pause. [E5]

evidence_cited.text: USGS HVO at image time: Kilauea ADVISORY/YELLOW in episodic_pause with Episode 55 ending 9:03 a.m. HST Oct 17, while Mauna Loa NORMAL/GREEN not erupting, favoring Kilauea as vog source.

Summit wind from NNE (30 deg at 16.7 km/h) blows toward SSW, consistent with pale veil extending southward from southern tip; downstream plume wind from ENE (71 deg at 37.8 km/h) continues southwestward transport.
Wind-aligned plume geometry: upwind end 50.3 km from Kilauea summit vs 69.0 km from Mauna Loa summit, centroid ~100 km south, 142-km veil, closer to and downwind of Kilauea.

Mask is 96.6% ocean (land_frac 0.034, minimal Hawaii overlap, no island swallowed), supporting over-water haze; visual pale blue-gray translucent veil distinct from surrounding bright white cumulus/cirrus.
No FIRMS fire clusters in plume bbox, excluding local wildfire smoke; strong Kilauea-summit volcanic thermal (316 marker pixels) confirms hot source persisting through pause.

classify.caveats: Kilauea was in episodic_pause (Episode 55 ended 9:03 a.m. HST same day), so plume is likely residual/degassing vog rather than vigorous eruptive plume; faint veil and modest wind shift between summit and plume add uncertainty.

kilauea.activity_summary: Episode 55 of the ongoing Halemaʻumaʻu eruption ended abruptly at 9:03 a.m. HST on October 17, 2026. VAN is being reissued to drop the alert level from WATCH to ADVISORY and the color code from ORANGE to YELLOW.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in September compared to August, and minor inflation continues. Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 53 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the September reporting period, after 87 in August. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.
